Tap an atom below to add it. Drag atoms together to bond in 2D, then press Combine to see it in 3D. Hold an atom to remove just that one. Double-tap a finished molecule to reset it. To change a bond to double, triple or four, tap the bond and use + and −. To build an ion, tap an atom, then use + and − to give it a charge.

How to use camera mode

  • Rotate: swipe on empty space. Pinch to zoom.
  • Move an atom: drag it. It springs back to its ideal angle. Drag the middle atom to move the whole molecule.
  • Reset: double-tap any atom to snap the molecule back to its most stable shape and position, and bring the view back to it.
  • Reveal information: tap the dark buttons at the bottom to light them up: Bonding Pair, Lone Pair (shows the lone pair clouds), Molecular and Electron Geometry, Formula (the AX code), Angle (shows the angle on the model) Bond polarity (orange arrows point toward the atom that pulls the bonding electrons harder, with red δ− and blue δ+ glows) and Molecular polarity (a dark arrow shows the pull of the whole molecule, and no dark arrow means the pulls cancel). Partial charges shows δ+ and δ− on each atom, and Electrostatic or Electron density colours the molecule’s surface. Tap again to hide. Closed a card by mistake? Turn its button off and on again.
  • Electronegativity: turn it on to show each atom’s Pauling value and how strong its pull is (weak, medium, strong, very strong) above the atom, plus a card explaining why. The hint line lists bond ΔEN values. Electronegativity describes how strongly an atom attracts shared bonding electrons. As a rough guide, ΔEN below 0.4 is nonpolar covalent, 0.4 up to about 1.7 is polar covalent, and 1.8 or more has ionic character; these cutoffs are approximate, and C–H is counted as nonpolar. The bond that pulls harder makes its atom slightly negative (δ−). Turn on Bond polarity to see arrows pointing toward the more electronegative atom, then Molecular polarity to see the whole molecule: if the arrows cancel because of a symmetric VSEPR shape the molecule is nonpolar, and if they do not it is polar. Source: Chemistry LibreTexts.
  • Several molecules: use the arrows at the top to see the others you made.
  • Leave: tap the crossed-out camera at the top.

Settings

Ionic compounds & polyatomic ions

Where to find this: open the Beaker (Ion creation) button, then tap the small ? help button at the bottom of the builder.

Ionic compound rules
  • Choose a positive ion (cation) and a negative ion (anion).
  • Balance the charges so the total charge is zero, using the smallest whole-number ratio.
  • Write the cation first, then the anion; use subscripts for counts greater than one.
  • This builder demonstrates charge-balanced formulas. It does not create a 3D molecule-like ionic bond.
NH₄⁺ (ammonium) rules
  • Ammonium contains one nitrogen and four hydrogens.
  • Draw four single N–H bonds. Nitrogen has no lone pair in this Lewis structure.
  • Put brackets around the structure and label the overall charge +1.
  • NH₄⁺ is an ion, not a free radical. A radical has an unpaired electron; charge and radical status are different properties.

Use Hints → Polyatomic ions to learn about an ion. Tap an ion card to see its atom-and-bond structure. Use the Beaker builder to balance ionic formulas.
